obs: "While various acts of limitation apply to the concerns of individuals, none of them operate against the government."

“for no laches is to be imputed to the government and against it no time runs so as to bar the public mights, which is no more nor less than another form of words for expressing the ancient rule of the common law, that time does, not run against the State.”

"It is upon this principle that in this country the statutes of a State prescribing periods within which rights must be prosecuted are not held to embrace the State itself, unless it is expressly designated or the mischiefs to be remedied are of such a nature that it must necessarily be included."
Weber v. Board of Harbor Commissioners
"Statutes of limitation are not for this reason held to embrace the State, unless she is expressly designated, or necessarily included by the nature of the mischiefs to be remedied."

"This case turns upon a statute of the State of Minnesota ... and the same limitation is applied by the statute to the State. The United States are not named in it." ... "In both it was held, without the intimation of a doubt, that a State statute cannot bar the United States."
United States v. Nashville, Chattanooga & St. Louis Railway Co.

"the United States, asserting rights vested in them as a sovereign government, are not bound by any statute of limitations, unless Congress has clearly manifested its intention that they should be so bound."
"As laches is not to be imputed to the Government, the statute of limitations does not apply to the State, unless it be clear from the act that it was intended to include the State"
Metropolitan Railroad v. District of Columbia
“No restrictive laws apply to the sovereign, unless so expressed. . . . such is the general law such the universal law, except where it is expressly waived.”

"The foundation of this rule is the proposition that time does not run against the government, that no statute of limitation affects the rights of the government, unless there is an express provision to that effect in the statute"
Miller v. Texas & Pacific Railway Co.
"Now supposing that the prerogative of the government prevented the statute from running until after the patent issued to the heirs of John Childress in June, 1868"

"the United States, asserting rights vested in them as a sovereign government, are not bound by any statute of limitations, unless Congress has clearly manifested its intention that they should be so bound."
United States v. American Bell Telephone Co.
“It is upon the principle of public policy that the United States have been held not bound by statutes of limitation unless Congress has clearly manifested that they should be so bound.”
"So the statute of limitations may be pleaded by the government, but not against it; nor is it affected by the laches of its officers."
"It would seem to follow from the general principle of law, so often asserted, that the statute of limitations does not run against the Government"
United States v. Whited & Wheless, Ltd.

"Fundamental to the interpretation of the statute which the answering of this question renders necessary, lies the rule of law settled \"as a great principle of public policy\" that the \"United States, asserting rights vested in them as a sovereign government, are not bound by any statute of limitations, unless Congress has clearly manifested its intention that they should be so bound,"
United States v. St. Paul, Minneapolis & Manitoba Railway Co.
“having regard to the general principle which requires a strict construction to be given to legislation in derogation of the public right”
Grand Trunk Western Railway Co. v. United States
"The statute of limitations does not ordinarily run against the United States"
E. I. Dupont De Nemours & Co. v. Davis
"Statutes of limitation sought to be applied to bar rights of the Government, must receive a strict construction in favor of the Government."
Bowers v. New York & Albany Lighterage Co.

"Undoubtedly the United States will not be held barred by a general statute of limitation unless, upon a strict construction in its favor, the United States and the claim sought to be enforced fairly may be held to be within the terms and purpose of the statute."
"*249 Under the established general rule a statute of limitation runs against the United States only when they assent and upon the conditions prescribed."
"The United States is not bound by state statutes of limitation unless Congress provides that it shall be."

"The Government's right to recover funds, from a person who received them by mistake and without right, is not barred unless Congress has 'clearly manifested its intention'[5] to raise a statutory barrier."
Guaranty Trust Co. v. United States
"The rule quod nullum tempus occurrit regi that the sovereign is exempt from the consequences of its laches, and from the operation of statutes of limitations"
Oklahoma Ex Rel. Johnson v. Cook
"The state court has also held that the statute of limitations does not run against the State in an action to enforce the statutory liability of the stockholders."
Block v. North Dakota Ex Rel. Board of University & School Lands
“The judicially created rule that a sovereign is normally exempt from the operation of a generally worded statute of limitations has retained its vigor …”
"Statutes of limitation sought to be applied to bar rights of the Government, must receive a strict construction in favor of the Government."
“The language of the statute admits of both interpretations. … [T]his Courts normal practice of construing ambiguous statutes of limitations in Government action in the Governments favor.”
Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation v. Environmental Protection Agency

“The principle that the United States are not bound by any statute of limitations, nor barred by any laches of their officers, however gross, in a suit brought by them as a sovereign Government to enforce a public right, or to assert a public interest, is established past all controversy or doubt.”
